title: Organic Isomerism Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
The same Lego bricks build a car or a house. The same letters spell listen and silent. Diya finds that ethanol and dimethyl ether are both C2H6O, yet one is a liquid boiling at 78 °C and the other a gas boiling at -24 °C. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 8, Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques) we see how the same atoms can make different compounds.

On the molecule bench, a carbon hops along a C5H12 chain to turn pentane into isopentane and neopentane while the atom counter stays at C 5 | H 12. An OH slides along propanol, an O hops into ethanol to make dimethyl ether, and an O slides along an ether chain to show metamerism. Then a stiff C=C refuses to twist (cis and trans but-2-ene) and a carbon with four different groups meets its mirror image. A worked example names the type for three pairs, then an exam trap, an original exam pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 82 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
